title: Our Kitchen & Joinery Design Process
tagline: From the first conversation to the final detail.
intro: Every home is different. So is every project.
At NURA Interiors, we bring design, materials and technical expertise together to create bespoke kitchens and architectural joinery that feel considered from the beginning.
Our six-stage approach helps you understand how your project develops, the decisions involved and what to expect along the way.
The exact scope, fees, deliverables, responsibilities and programme are confirmed in your written proposal and appointment.

sections.title: 01 : Tell Us About Your Project
blocks: **Every considered space begins with a conversation.**
Tell us about your home, the spaces you would like to transform and how you want to use them.
Share your ideas, priorities and any existing plans, photographs or material references. Your property location, approximate budget and preferred timing also help us understand what may be possible.
We review your brief, discuss the services you may need and explain the appropriate next steps.
Before commissioned design work begins, we clarify the proposed design scope, any applicable fees and what your appointment would include.
**What to bring:** Your property location, available plans or photographs, design references, approximate budget and preferred timeline.
**What happens next:** We identify the information needed to establish the scope and discuss the appropriate commercial next step, including whether an initial budget indication is possible.

sections.title: 02 : Develop the Design
blocks: **Thoughtful design brings together the way a space looks and the way it works.**
We explore layouts, storage, proportions and material combinations, considering how each decision contributes to the wider interior.
Whether you are planning a bespoke kitchen, fitted wardrobes or architectural joinery, the design develops around your priorities and the practical requirements of the space.
Within your agreed appointment, we prepare the relevant design proposals and review them with you. Feedback helps refine the direction before technical details are progressed.
Your written appointment confirms which drawings, visualisations, material selections and design revisions are included.
**What NURA does:** Develops the agreed design proposals and explains the practical implications of the options.
**What we agree together:** The preferred design direction, applicable deliverables, outstanding decisions and approval process.

sections.title: 03 : Refine the Technical Details
blocks: **The smallest details can make the greatest difference.**
Once the design direction is established, we turn our attention to the dimensions, specifications and interfaces that bring the design closer to manufacture.
This may include cabinetry construction, internal fittings, door profiles, finishes, hardware and the relationship with appliances, worktops, lighting and surrounding architectural features.
Where required, we coordinate the agreed joinery information with your architect, interior designer, contractor and specialist suppliers.
Before manufacture, responsibilities for site measurements, technical checks, product information and final approvals are identified and confirmed.
**What NURA does:** Develops and coordinates the technical information included in its appointment.
**What we confirm together:** The approved specification, outstanding technical decisions and who is responsible for checking and approving each requirement.

sections.title: 04 : Confirm the Scope & Programme
blocks: **Confidence comes from knowing what has been agreed.**
Before the project moves into the next committed stage, we bring together the relevant design, technical and commercial information.
Your written proposal sets out the agreed scope, quotation and programme, including the applicable arrangements for manufacture, delivery and installation.
We review what is included, what is excluded and which responsibilities belong to other members of your project team.
Any changes to approved designs, materials or specifications may affect the price or programme. The process for reviewing and authorising those changes is agreed before they are carried out.
**What we confirm in writing:**

- The agreed design and specification
- Scope of supply and installation
- Quotation, applicable VAT and payment stages
- Programme and relevant dependencies
- Exclusions and responsibilities of other trades
- Final approvals and the process for managing changes
The project proceeds in accordance with the agreed appointment and commercial terms.

sections.title: 05 : Coordinate Manufacture & Installation
blocks: **Carefully developed details deserve carefully coordinated delivery.**
With the required approvals in place, the project progresses towards manufacture and installation.
We coordinate the relevant production, delivery and fitting requirements within our agreed scope, working with the appointed manufacturing and installation teams as appropriate.
Approved specifications and applicable quality checks help guide the work as it moves from technical information to finished cabinetry.
Installation also depends on the readiness of the site. Access, building conditions, services, protection and the work of other trades must be coordinated with the relevant parties.
We communicate the requirements within our responsibility and identify decisions or changes that could affect delivery, installation or the agreed programme.
**What NURA does:** Coordinates the manufacture and installation activities included in its appointment.
**What your project team does:** Manages the site preparations, access and other trade responsibilities allocated to them.
**What we confirm together:** Site readiness, installation arrangements, responsibilities and any changes affecting cost or timing.

sections.title: 06 : Review & Handover
blocks: **The finishing details matter just as much as the first ideas.**
As the agreed work reaches completion, we review the finished cabinetry and joinery with you.
This provides an opportunity to discuss the result, identify any outstanding items and answer questions about finishes, operation and ongoing care.
Any items requiring attention are recorded, together with the agreed responsibilities and follow-up arrangements.
We also explain the applicable warranty terms and how to contact NURA if you need assistance after completion.

NURA-made cabinetry specified in your contract is supported by our **10-year cabinetry guarantee** against covered manufacturing and material defects. Hardware, appliances, worktops and installation are subject to their respective contractual terms.
[Explore Our 10-Year Cabinetry Guarantee](/guarantee)
**At handover, we confirm:** The completed scope, outstanding items, relevant care guidance and the appropriate contact for aftercare.

sections.title: Questions Before You Begin
blocks: ### How long will my kitchen or joinery project take?
Every project has its own requirements.
The programme depends on the scope, design approvals, selected materials, manufacturing requirements and site readiness.
We discuss the likely stages against your brief and confirm the relevant programme as part of the agreed project arrangements.
Changes to dimensions, finishes, appliances or site conditions may affect the sequence or completion dates.
### How much will my project cost?
The cost depends on the scale of the work, cabinetry construction, materials, hardware, technical requirements and installation arrangements.
Share your approximate budget during the initial conversation so we can discuss an appropriate direction.
We clarify applicable design fees before commissioned design work begins. The project quotation and payment terms are confirmed in writing according to the agreed scope.
### What will my design appointment include?
The deliverables depend on the services you commission.
Your written appointment identifies the relevant design proposals, drawings, specifications, material selections, revisions and coordination responsibilities.
This helps establish what you will receive and which decisions must be approved before the next stage.
### Can NURA work with my architect, interior designer or builder?
Yes. We work with homeowners and design professionals to develop and coordinate the joinery requirements relevant to each project.
Share your latest drawings, project stage and the details of your appointed team.
We can then discuss the coordination required and agree the relevant responsibilities.
### Do I need completed plans before contacting NURA?
No.
You can begin with photographs, inspiration, a description of your home and an outline of what you would like to achieve.
Available plans and measurements are helpful, but you do not need every detail resolved before your first conversation.
### What happens after installation?
We review the agreed work, discuss any outstanding items and provide relevant care and aftercare information.
The warranty coverage, exclusions and support arrangements applicable to your project are recorded in your written contract.

sections.title: Let’s Discuss Your Project
blocks: **A room can change a life.**
Whether you are planning a bespoke kitchen, architectural joinery or a coordinated approach across several rooms, we would be pleased to hear what you have in mind.
Share your ideas, property location, available plans and approximate budget. Our studio will review your enquiry and discuss a suitable next step.
